claimedEvidence.claim:
review-candidate.patch applies cleanly but is NOT safe to merge. Two real problems: it breaks a deliberately pinned contract test (verified: 1 of 6 tests fails after applying), and it does not actually deliver the "30 minutes of inactivity" it claims, because nothing in the service tracks activity — expiry is measured from session creation only (service.py:44), so shortening the constant to 30 minutes makes every session die 30 minutes after it is created, active or not. The comment it deletes says "do not change without a contract decision", and tests/test_service.py:15 records that decision (2024-06: 24h) on purpose. Notably, the sibling patches/main-moved.patch in this same repo passes all 6 tests while giving ops an override — that is the shape of the fix that respects the contract.

Applying review-candidate.patch (which sets 30*60) and running `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` yields 'AssertionError: 1800 != 86400' — 1 failure out of 6. The patch also deletes the line-12 warning 'do not change without a contract decision' instead of recording a new decision, so the merge ships a red suite and silently overrides a documented team decision.", "fix": "Either get the contract decision reversed and update test_session_ttl_is_24h in the same change, or adopt the approach already in patches/main-moved.patch (env override KEEPNOTE_TTL_SECONDS defaulting to 24*60*60), which I verified passes all 6 tests."},
